unit.title: Empirical Entropy as a Trustworthy Software Component
unit.scope: A self-contained first encounter with discrete empirical entropy through a tested, streaming byte-analysis utility.
prerequisites: Comfort with sums, logarithms, and finite probability distributions
Ability to implement and test a small Python 3 program
learning_objectives: Compute a finite empirical distribution from event counts and evaluate base-2 Shannon entropy
Turn mathematical preconditions and edge cases into an explicit software contract
Implement bounded-memory binary-file analysis with deterministic machine-readable output
Use focused tests to check numerical properties, invalid inputs, and I/O boundaries
State what empirical entropy does and does not establish about compression or security

unit_completion_requires: All four learner artifacts exist and are inspectable
The implementation and learner tests run in the declared Python environment
Deterministic evaluator checks cover the public contract, numerical cases, binary I/O, and error behavior
Comprehension responses are independently assessed against examiner-only criteria
completion_policy.validation_authority: Only an independent worker-harness-controlled evaluator may promote the unit to completed.
completion_policy.future_course_completion: Requires separately sourced, classified, scheduled, completed, and independently validated later units; no such claim is made here.
